stories.headline: Lai rejects being 'traded away' after Trump calls US arms sales a China bargaining chip following Beijing summit
stories.summary: Following Trump's two-day state visit to China (May 14–15), during which he described pending US arms sales to Taiwan as a 'very good negotiating chip' with Beijing and cautioned Taiwan against declaring independence, President Lai Ching-te issued a five-point Facebook statement and spoke at the DPP's 40th anniversary event insisting Taiwan 'will never be sacrificed or traded' and that US arms sales are a legal commitment. Taiwan's Foreign Ministry, National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu, and Representative to the US Alexander Yui reinforced the message in public statements and television appearances. China's Taiwan Affairs Office condemned Lai's remarks as 'lies.' Trump also discussed arms sales with Xi but said he had made no commitments; he separately expressed pessimism about gaining Jimmy Lai's release from Hong Kong prison after raising the issue with Xi.

stories.headline: TSMC reports strong Q1 results, approves $20B Arizona capital boost, and sells down Vanguard stake
stories.summary: TSMC's board (May 12) approved a capital injection of up to US$20 billion into its Arizona subsidiary as part of a $165 billion US investment plan, while Q1 2026 financials showed net income of NT$572.5 billion and raised the quarterly dividend to a record NT$7. Separately, on May 15 TSMC announced plans to sell up to 152 million shares (≈8.1% stake) in Vanguard International Semiconductor via block trade, reducing its holding to ≈19%; analysts read this as a capital reallocation toward AI-era investments. TSMC's Arizona and Japan (JASM) fabs both reported profits in Q1 for the first time. Institutional investors including Tiger Global, Eminence Capital, and Appaloosa added to TSM positions while Driehaus Capital and others trimmed.

stories.headline: KMT-TPP opposition passes reduced NT$780B defense budget, cutting domestic drone funding; legislative session extended
stories.summary: On May 9, the KMT and TPP used their legislative majority to pass a NT$780 billion supplementary defense budget — substantially less than the NT$1.25 trillion requested by the Lai administration — in a 59-0 vote with 48 DPP abstentions. The approved package excluded domestic drone production funds and other asymmetric-defense line items. The DPP accused the KMT of deliberately undermining Taiwan's indigenous defense industry to please Beijing. In a related move, the legislature voted to extend the current session through August 31 over what the opposition called DPP budget negligence. Premier Cho Jung-tai was summoned to present the administration's defense purchase plan to the legislature on Tuesday.

stories.headline: KMT chair's China visit, cross-strait stance, and planned US trip draw fire from DPP and MAC
stories.summary: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun's recent meeting with Xi Jinping and her public statements calling for replacement of the 'first island chain' concept with a 'chain of peace and prosperity' drew sharp criticism from Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, which accused her of echoing Chinese propaganda. KMT Vice Chairman Chang Jung-kung separately met CCP's fourth-ranked official Wang Huning at a cross-strait cultural summit in Beijing. Reports also emerged that Cheng's planned 14-person US trip may be seeking funding from overseas Taiwanese groups; the KMT denied this. Two US congressmen (Tiffany and Smith) wrote Secretary Rubio urging that President Lai receive the same US visit rights as KMT chair Cheng.

stories.headline: DPP nominates legislator Puma Shen as candidate for Taipei mayoral race against KMT incumbent
stories.summary: President and DPP Chair Lai Ching-te formally announced on May 13 that legislator Puma Shen (Shen Po-yang) would be the party's candidate in the November Taipei mayoral election, where he faces incumbent KMT Mayor Chiang Wan-an. Shen's campaign team had quietly begun operations beforehand. The DPP also outlined its strategy focused on Taipei residents' needs; the last time DPP won the Taipei mayorship was decades ago.

stories.headline: Lai addresses Copenhagen Democracy Summit and cites China's obstruction of Eswatini trip as proof of authoritarianism; NYT reveals flight security details
stories.summary: President Lai Ching-te delivered a video address to the Copenhagen Democracy Summit on May 12, citing Chinese interference with his April flight to Eswatini as evidence of consolidating authoritarianism and calling on democracies to unite. He also pre-summit thanked the US for defense support from Copenhagen. The New York Times (May 14) published new details of the 'secret mission' logistics — satellite phones, a borrowed royal aircraft — that allowed Lai to reach Eswatini despite Chinese pressure blocking normal routing. Separately, commentators debated Lai's May 8 attendance at a ceremony honoring Japanese colonial-era engineer Hatta, which Beijing and domestic critics called politically provocative.

stories.headline: Opposition legislature moves to impeach President Lai; May 19 vote scheduled
stories.summary: Taiwan's KMT- and TPP-controlled legislature is set to vote on Tuesday (May 19) on a motion to impeach President Lai Ching-te — a largely symbolic measure that cannot pass without a two-thirds majority unavailable to the opposition. Lai did not attend a second legislative hearing on the impeachment motion, drawing criticism from KMT and TPP lawmakers who accused him of dodging democratic accountability. Opposition legislators cited Lai's alleged dereliction of duty and unconstitutional actions, including his December refusal to submit nominees for the Constitutional Court.

stories.headline: Canadian Conservative MP Chong visits Taipei to meet President Lai despite China's warning to parliamentarians
stories.summary: Canadian Conservative foreign affairs critic Michael Chong arrived in Taipei on Monday and was scheduled to meet President Lai Ching-te on Wednesday, defying a recent warning from China's ambassador to Canada against parliamentary visits to Taiwan. The visit followed an earlier January incident in which two Liberal MPs cut short a Taiwan trip before meeting Lai after a Chinese diplomatic warning.
